1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. RDS: Relational Database Service; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud; AZ: Availability Zone; DMS: Database Migration Service; SCT: Schema Conversion Tool; DB: database; CLI: command line interface; DAX: DynamoDB Accelerator; OSS: open source software; SPARQL: SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language

  • Explain why a managed database such as Amazon RDS beats one you run on EC2
  • Tell Multi-AZ deployments from read replicas, and say what Amazon Aurora adds
  • Recognize Amazon DynamoDB for NoSQL and Amazon ElastiCache for in-memory speed
  • Place Amazon DocumentDB and Amazon Neptune
  • Use AWS DMS and AWS SCT to migrate a database

2Relational, NoSQL and in-memory databases

Running case

Tidewater's Data Needs Differ

  • The order database runs on a server the team patches and backs up itself, often on weekends
  • The product catalog needs simple lookups in milliseconds, even at the sale peak
  • The same popular product pages are read thousands of times a minute
  • A recommendation idea needs to follow links between customers, orders and products
  • An old Oracle database must move to AWS with little downtime
  • Your job: choose the database for each need

Database Types at a Glance

  • Relational: data in tables, queried with SQL: Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora
  • Key-value NoSQL: simple, fast lookups at any scale: Amazon DynamoDB
  • Document: JSON-like documents, MongoDB-compatible: Amazon DocumentDB
  • In-memory: data and caches held in memory: Amazon ElastiCache
  • Graph: relationships between things: Amazon Neptune

Exam tip

Name the data model first: tables, key-value, documents, memory or relationships.

Self-Managed or Managed: Databases on EC2 and Amazon RDS

Task Database on EC2 Amazon RDS
Install and patch the database software You AWS
Patch the operating system You AWS
Backups, scaling, high availability You AWS
Query tuning and application design You You
Hardware, power and cooling AWS AWS
  • Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service) runs Db2, MariaDB, SQL Server, MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL, plus Aurora
  • AWS recommends RDS as the default for most relational workloads
Exam tip

Less administration: Amazon RDS. Full control of the database server: EC2.

RDS Multi-AZ and Read Replicas

  • Multi-AZ: RDS keeps a standby in another Availability Zone, copied synchronously, and fails over automatically
  • A Multi-AZ DB instance standby does not serve reads; a Multi-AZ DB cluster has readable standbys
  • Read replicas are read-only copies, updated asynchronously, that scale reads and run reports
  • A replica can be in another Region and can be promoted to a standalone instance for disaster recovery
  • RDS does not autoscale replicas: you create them

Exam tip

Availability and failover: Multi-AZ. Read scaling: read replicas.

Amazon Aurora: Relational Built for the Cloud [Verify live]

  • Amazon Aurora is a fully managed relational engine compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL
  • It is part of Amazon RDS: the same console, CLI and API handle provisioning, patching, backup, recovery and failure detection
  • AWS states throughput of up to 6 times stock MySQL and stock PostgreSQL on similar hardware
  • Storage grows automatically, up to 256 TiB for a cluster volume
  • It automates clustering and replication, usually the hardest parts of database administration
  • You can move from RDS for MySQL or PostgreSQL with a snapshot or one-way replication
  • As of 4 November 2026: figures are from the Aurora User Guide
Exam tip

MySQL or PostgreSQL compatible, with higher performance and storage that grows by itself: Aurora.

Amazon DynamoDB: Serverless NoSQL

  • Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless, fully managed NoSQL database for key-value and document data
  • Single-digit millisecond performance at any scale
  • No servers to provision or patch, and no maintenance windows
  • On-demand capacity charges per request and scales up and down; provisioned capacity is the alternative
  • Data is copied across three Availability Zones by default, and global tables replicate across Regions
  • Data is encrypted at rest by default, with point-in-time recovery for up to 35 days
  • DAX adds an in-memory cache, from milliseconds to microseconds
  • DynamoDB has no JOIN operator
Exam tip

Key-value lookups, milliseconds at any scale, no servers: Amazon DynamoDB.

Amazon ElastiCache: In-Memory Caching

  • Amazon ElastiCache is a managed in-memory data store and cache
  • Its engines are Valkey, Memcached and Redis OSS
  • Put it in front of a database, so popular reads come from memory: faster for users, less load on the database
  • ElastiCache Serverless needs only a name; node-based clusters give control over node type, count and Availability Zones
  • AWS manages hardware, monitoring, node replacement and patching

Exam tip

Speed up repeated reads with an in-memory cache: Amazon ElastiCache.

3Document, graph, migration and practice

Amazon DocumentDB and Amazon Neptune

Service What it is Remember
Amazon DocumentDB Fully managed document database, compatible with MongoDB: same code, drivers and tools; storage grows automatically; up to 15 replicas; backups up to 35 days JSON-like documents
Amazon Neptune Fully managed graph database for highly connected data; queries in Gremlin, openCypher and SPARQL; recommendation engines, fraud detection, knowledge graphs; up to 15 read replicas Relationships
Exam tip

MongoDB workloads: DocumentDB. Recommendations from relationships: Neptune.

Moving Databases: AWS DMS and AWS SCT

  • AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) migrates databases and data stores to AWS, or between cloud and on-premises
  • It can do a one-time migration or replicate ongoing changes to keep source and target in sync
  • It supports same-engine and different-engine migrations
  • AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) converts the schema and code from one engine to another, such as Oracle to PostgreSQL
  • DMS Schema Conversion can also convert source schemas

Exam tip

Different engine: SCT converts the schema, DMS moves the data.

What the Exam Asks: Databases

  • EC2 or RDS: you run the database, or AWS manages it
  • Multi-AZ or read replica: failover, or more read capacity
  • RDS or Aurora: standard engines, or MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible with cloud-built storage
  • DynamoDB: key-value lookups with no servers
  • ElastiCache: an in-memory cache for repeated reads
  • DocumentDB or Neptune: MongoDB documents, or connected data
  • SCT or DMS: convert the schema, or move the data
Exam tip

Match the data model and the management you want to the service.

Design Check: Tidewater's Database Plan

Tidewater's need Choose
The order database, without weekend patching Amazon RDS
Keep running if a data center fails Multi-AZ deployment
Reports slowing the order database A read replica
MySQL compatible, with storage that grows itself Amazon Aurora
Catalog lookups in milliseconds at any scale Amazon DynamoDB
Product pages read thousands of times a minute Amazon ElastiCache
Recommendations from links between customers and products Amazon Neptune
An old Oracle database to PostgreSQL SCT to convert, DMS to move
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Tidewater runs a MySQL database on an EC2 instance and wants AWS to handle patching, backups and failover. Which service fits best?

  • AAmazon DynamoDB, a serverless key-value database
  • BAmazon ElastiCache, an in-memory data store
  • CAmazon RDS for MySQL, a managed relational database
  • DAmazon Neptune, a managed graph database
Show the answer

Answer: C. Amazon RDS runs MySQL as a managed service, so AWS handles database and operating system patching, backups and failover. DynamoDB, ElastiCache and Neptune use different data models and would not run the existing MySQL database.

S2Tidewater's order database must stay available if one Availability Zone fails. Which RDS feature meets this need?

  • AA Multi-AZ deployment with a synchronous standby in another zone
  • BA read replica that serves the reporting queries
  • CA larger DB instance class with more memory and CPU
  • DA manual snapshot taken each night and stored in S3
Show the answer

Answer: A. A Multi-AZ deployment keeps a synchronous standby in another Availability Zone and fails over automatically. A read replica scales reads, a bigger instance does not remove the single zone, and a nightly snapshot restores slowly with data loss.

S3The product catalog must answer simple key lookups with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, with no servers to manage. Which service fits best?

  • AAmazon RDS for PostgreSQL, with a Multi-AZ standby
  • BAmazon DynamoDB, with on-demand capacity
  • CAmazon Neptune, with graph queries
  • DAmazon Aurora, with MySQL compatibility
Show the answer

Answer: B. DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale and no servers to manage. RDS and Aurora are relational engines with instances to size, and Neptune is built for connected data.

S4The same product pages are read thousands of times a minute and slow the database. Which service can serve those repeated reads from memory?

  • AAmazon DocumentDB, a MongoDB-compatible database
  • BAWS Database Migration Service, a data mover
  • CAWS Schema Conversion Tool, a schema converter
  • DAmazon ElastiCache, a managed in-memory cache
Show the answer

Answer: D. ElastiCache is a managed in-memory data store and cache, so repeated reads come from memory and the database does less work. DocumentDB stores documents, and DMS and SCT are migration tools.

S5Tidewater is moving an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Which TWO services help? (Select TWO.)

  • AAWS Schema Conversion Tool, to convert the schema and code
  • BAmazon ElastiCache, to cache the Oracle data
  • CAWS Database Migration Service, to move and replicate the data
  • DAmazon Neptune, to store the converted relationships
  • EAWS Backup, to schedule the nightly copies
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Moving between different engines needs the schema converted, which AWS SCT does, and the data moved, which AWS DMS does. ElastiCache is a cache, Neptune is a graph database, and AWS Backup protects data rather than migrating it.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Managed or not RDS patches, backs up and fails over; on EC2 you do it all
Availability and reads Multi-AZ fails over; read replicas scale reads; Aurora is MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible
NoSQL and speed DynamoDB for key-value at any scale; ElastiCache for in-memory caching
Specialist engines DocumentDB for MongoDB documents; Neptune for graphs
Migration SCT converts the schema; DMS moves the data
